title: 2026–27 KOICA Youth Leaders Program identity
text: The current website should present the programme as the 2026–27 KOICA Youth Leaders Program (YLP). It is jointly operated by KOICA and Hallym University. Where programme partner logos are shown together, the intended order is KOICA, Hallym University, then the CIAT/KOICA Fellowship Program mark.

title: Hallym University partnership
text: Hallym University is the partner university jointly operating the KOICA Youth Leaders Program with KOICA. Programme and curriculum questions may be handled through the partner-university contact channels published for the cohort.

title: Public and Private Sector outcome emphasis
text: The Public Sector and Private Sector tracks should be clearly separated in the participant journey. The Public Sector places stronger emphasis on solving public issues, public governance, policy, and digital-government improvement. The Private Sector places stronger emphasis on employment, career opportunities, entrepreneurship, product development, and practical market-facing solutions. Applicants should enter and apply through the track that matches their background and goals.

title: KOICA Youth Leaders Program overview
text: The KOICA Youth Leaders Program (YLP) supports young leaders from Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, and Cameroon to strengthen leadership, governance, digital transformation, innovation, AI, and digital skills. The programme connects participants across five West African countries and combines shared learning with sector-specific training. Cohort-specific dates, selection details, and application requirements can change, so the current cohort announcement should always be treated as the final authority.

title: Participating countries
text: The KOICA Youth Leaders Program serves participants from five West African countries: Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, and Cameroon. Regional KOICA offices are important points of contact for application and eligibility questions.

title: Three programme phases
text: Each cohort follows a three-stage journey: 1) Online Training, a common virtual foundation for both tracks covering leadership, governance, AI, and digital skills; 2) Local Training in Ghana, an on-site sector-specific practical phase where participants develop Action Plans; and 3) Invitational Training in the Republic of Korea, an advanced training and exposure phase for outstanding trainees from both tracks. Exact dates are announced per cohort.

title: Public Sector track
text: The Public Sector track is designed for government officials, policy practitioners, and public-sector employees. Its focus includes strengthening public governance, policy planning and development, AI-driven digital-government innovation (DX/AX), and Action Plans that participants can take back to their institutions. Participant numbers are indicative and may vary by cohort.

title: Private Sector track
text: The Private Sector track is designed for aspiring entrepreneurs, developers, startup founders, and academic professionals. Its focus includes startup capability building, customer journey mapping, MVP design and validation, no-code AI applications, and practical Action Plans. Participant numbers are indicative and may vary by cohort.

title: Choosing the correct track
text: Applicants should choose the single track that best matches their background. Public Sector is for applicants working in government or qualifying public institutions. Private Sector is for entrepreneurs, developers, startup founders, academic professionals, and other qualifying private-sector profiles. Each track has its own application form.

title: Required eligibility criteria
text: General required criteria shown on the YLP website are: age 19 to 34; working in the public sector, private sector, or academia; interest in leadership and digital innovation; English communication skills; availability for local training in Ghana; and eligibility for visa issuance for Ghana and the Republic of Korea. Cohort announcements may adjust details, so applicants should confirm the current announcement before applying.

title: Priority consideration
text: Priority consideration may include an associate degree or higher or at least two years of relevant work experience. Female applicants and applicants from rural areas are encouraged to apply. Public Sector priority includes policy-planning practitioners. Private Sector priority includes early-stage startup entrepreneurs focused on solving local issues.

title: Preferred applicant strengths
text: Preferred strengths include experience in AI or ICT, strong willingness to participate in team projects, experience in public policy or entrepreneurship, and commitment to sharing knowledge with colleagues after returning home. These strengths improve an application but are separate from the required eligibility criteria.

title: Students and borderline eligibility
text: The general criteria focus on applicants aged 19 to 34 who are working in the public sector, private sector, or academia. Final-year student status is not automatically resolved by the general guidance. Applicants whose work or academic status is unclear should confirm directly with their regional KOICA office before applying.

title: Current website application flow
text: When applications are open, the public Apply page provides a separate downloadable application form for the Public Sector and Private Sector tracks. Applicants should download the correct form, complete it, return to the Apply page, enter the requested applicant details, upload the completed document, and submit it through the website. When applications are closed, form downloads and application submissions are disabled.

title: Application documents
text: General application guidance may require the KOICA Application Form, a Letter of Recommendation, a passport copy or national ID where the cohort announcement allows it, and the Agreement on Provision of Personal Information. Documents should be signed where indicated. The current application form and cohort announcement override older or general document lists.

title: Submitting a completed application online
text: The website's in-app submission form asks for the applicant's full name, email address, phone number, country, organization or institution, application track, and completed application document. The site accepts PDF, DOC, or DOCX application files up to 10 MB. After a successful submission, the applicant receives a unique application reference and should keep it for their records.

title: Screening and final selection
text: The general selection process has two stages: the regional KOICA office performs initial screening and shortlisting, and the partner university conducts a second document review and final selection. Results are communicated individually by email according to the cohort timeline. Applicants should monitor their email closely after applying.

title: What happens after selection
text: Final selected participants may be asked to submit a recent medical check-up certificate by the communicated deadline. Selected participants then receive immigration and departure support for training in Ghana and Korea. Curriculum and programme questions can be directed to the partner university.

title: Application open and closed status
text: The website clearly shows whether applications are currently open or closed. When closed, downloads and submissions are disabled. Applicants should follow the regional KOICA office for the next application window and current cohort announcement. The chatbot should not invent an application deadline if no current deadline is present in retrieved programme data.

title: Programme language
text: The programme is conducted in English. English communication ability is therefore part of the general eligibility criteria. Participants need enough English to learn, collaborate on team projects, communicate with facilitators, and present their work.

title: Programme costs and funding
text: KOICA training programmes are development-cooperation initiatives funded by the Korean government. The exact costs, allowances, travel items, or expenses covered can differ by cohort. Applicants should rely on the current cohort announcement or regional KOICA office for a definitive list of covered costs.

title: Visa eligibility and support
text: Applicants must generally be eligible for visa issuance for both Ghana and the Republic of Korea. Final selected participants receive immigration and departure support for the training phases. Visa requirements and documentation should be confirmed against the current cohort instructions.

title: After the programme
text: After the programme, participants can remain involved through KOICA Club activities in their home countries, the KOICA Fellowship Community, regional networking across the five participating countries, and community-service initiatives that share knowledge and skills back home.

title: Application and submission support
text: Application, eligibility, and submission questions should be confirmed with the applicant's regional KOICA office. For Ghana-related application support, the website lists koicaghanaaciat@gmail.com. Official cohort announcements and instructions from the regional KOICA office override general website guidance.

title: Curriculum and programme support
text: Questions about curriculum, training content, and the programme itself can be directed to the partner university. The website lists KOICAYLP@hallym.ac.kr for programme inquiries.

title: Participant learning portal
text: Registered participants can sign in to the YLP portal using their registered name and KOICA PIN. The portal provides the participant dashboard, programme calendar, modules, learning progress, announcements, presentation materials, and resources for the participant's track. PIN or access problems should be raised with the appropriate programme administrator or regional KOICA office.

title: What Peko can answer
text: Peko is the KOICA YLP website assistant. Peko should answer only from the YLP knowledge base and current programme data. It can help with programme overview, participating countries, tracks, eligibility, application steps, submission requirements, schedule, training sessions, resources, visas, general cost guidance, contacts, and alumni information. If the knowledge base does not support an answer, Peko should say so and direct the user to the regional KOICA office or partner university rather than guessing.
